subject.title: Update to 2026.7.1 left managed install and WhatsApp plugin linked to old embedded Node

question: Which component should own unsupported embedded-Node upgrades and the resumable handoff back into OpenClaw doctor, plugin repair, and gateway verification for install-cli managed prefixes?
rationale: The observable bug spans the openclaw.ai runtime installer and OpenClaw's update, doctor, service, and plugin-repair paths; choosing ownership and rollback semantics is necessary before a safe implementation boundary is clear.

options.title: Installer-owned atomic handoff
options.body: Have OpenClaw detect the managed-prefix layout, invoke a versioned installer repair protocol, then resume doctor, plugin repair, and gateway verification from the new runtime with rollback metadata.

options.title: Core-owned runtime upgrade
options.body: Teach openclaw update to download and replace embedded Node itself, accepting duplicated runtime-install and platform-verification responsibilities in core.

options.title: Guided fail-early recovery
options.body: Stop before package mutation and surface a single in-product repair launcher that reruns the installer and automatically resumes update repair afterward.

recommendation.title: Installer-owned atomic handoff
recommendation.body: Have OpenClaw detect the managed-prefix layout, invoke a versioned installer repair protocol, then resume doctor, plugin repair, and gateway verification from the new runtime with rollback metadata.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history most directly connects this contributor to managed update and plugin synchronization behavior across the affected path.
